title: Pundalik's brick
hookLine: a knock at the door while a son is washing his parents' feet, and a brick tossed out for God to stand on
carry: serving your parents is serving God
tomorrow: why would an old man call a god 'mother'?
last: THE WARI: THE WALKING AND SINGING ARE THE WORSHIP.

lines: A SON WASHING HIS PARENTS' FEET.
cards: There's a knock at the door. The young man inside doesn't get up. He's kneeling by his old father and mother, washing their feet, and his hands are busy.
The visitor, the story says, is God himself, come all the way from far off to see him.

Without leaving his parents, the young man reaches for the nearest thing, a brick, tosses it out through the doorway, and says: please, stand on this, and wait. I'll be with you when I'm done. That's Pundalik.
And that brick is why Vitthal stands the way he does.

teach.b: Varkaris tell it like this. Pundalik, in some tellings, wasn't always a good son. He had neglected his parents, until something turned him around, and from then on he served them with his whole heart.
That service is what draws God to Pandharpur. Krishna, the story says, comes looking for him, because a devotion like that is worth the journey. And Pundalik makes him wait.
A listener might expect everything to be dropped when God arrives. Here, the son finishes caring for his parents first, and the god of the story doesn't mind.
He steps onto the brick, puts his hands on his hips, and waits.

teach.h: STANDING ON A BRICK, HANDS ON HIPS
teach.b: That's the shape of Vitthal's image at Pandharpur: standing on a brick, hands on hips, patient. Varkaris say he's still standing there, still waiting, for Pundalik and for everyone who comes after. So where is God found?
Not only at a shrine. In a basin of water and two tired old pairs of feet. Pundalik doesn't choose between serving his parents and loving God.
To him the serving is the loving, and God agrees by waiting. It's an old Hindu teaching, not a one-off.

teach.h: LET YOUR MOTHER BE A GOD TO YOU
teach.b: In the Taittiriya Upanishad, a teacher sends students home with: let your mother be a god to you; let your father be a god to you.
Pundalik lived it, and the god of Pandharpur still stands on the brick, saying: take your time, I'm here.

how: Varkaris retell the story of Pundalik, and pilgrims at Pandharpur visit his shrine as well as Vitthal's, the god who stands on a brick with hands on hips.

o: the walkers who leave their parents behind to go and serve God
the walkers whose god stands on a brick at Pandharpur, waiting
the walkers who carry bricks to build Vitthal's temple each year

games.q: Pundalik and the brick — tap the pairs.
p: tossed out for God to stand on
God, come to see a devoted son

s: in the story, Pundalik drops everything the moment God arrives
he keeps caring for his parents and asks God to wait on a brick.
Vitthal's image at Pandharpur stands on a brick with hands on hips
the pose the story explains: a god patiently waiting.
every telling says Pundalik was a perfect son from the start
some tellings say he once neglected his parents before he turned around.

games.q: your grandfather needs help with his shoes right as the evening prayer at the temple begins. by Pundalik's story, what fits?
o: help him first; the help is the prayer, and God can wait on a brick.
go to the prayer; God should always come before chores.
rush the shoes so you can make the prayer, half-listening to him.
games.why: Pundalik kept washing his parents' feet and gave God a brick to wait on. to him the serving was the loving, and Varkaris say God still waits there.

practice: Bring to mind someone you look after, or someone who once looked after you: their hands, their feet, the way they move when they're tired.

Picture one small thing you do for them, setting down a glass of water, helping with a coat, and stay with it slowly. If you pray, you can let that small act be your prayer, the way it was for Pundalik.

wordCard.voice: Maharashtra's Varkari. The tradition whose god stands on Pundalik's brick at Pandharpur, hands on hips, still waiting. Today's word.

orig.note: Pundalik in Marathi, written in Devanagari: the son whose brick Vitthal stands on.

carryVoice: Carry this: serving your parents is serving God. A god waits on a brick while love finishes its work. That's today, done.
